# Auto-Generated Tournament News + Personalized Learn

The user's idea: when a player registers for a tournament, they should see news specifically about
that tournament - and if someone hits a century or wins a match for their team, an article should
be automatically generated telling that story, visible to every player in the tournament. Built in
this pass, alongside a smaller companion feature for the Learn section: personalized lesson
recommendations driven by a player's own weak line/length data (already computed by the tendency-
analytics system built earlier for shot advice/bowling plans). Global/international cricket news
was explicitly scoped as a **future** addition, not built now - see "Deliberately not built" below.

## Auto-generated tournament news (`d396e8b`, `dc1b96a`, `dee6a09`)

### How an article gets written

New `backend/src/services/matchArticleGenerator.js`. When a tournament-linked match transitions to
`Completed` (hooked into the existing `matchController.updateMatch`, wrapped in try/catch so a bug
here can never fail match completion itself), it does a single ball-by-ball pass over the match
(`computeMatchPerformances`) building a per-player breakdown for *this match only* - runs, balls,
fours, sixes, wickets, economy, and whether they took a hat-trick (3 consecutive credited wickets in
their own legal-ball sequence, same detection logic tendencyAnalytics.js already uses for the
hat-trick achievement badge).

From that, `pickHeroMoment` picks the single most newsworthy story in priority order: century (100+)
> five-wicket haul > hat-trick > half-century (best of, not first-found) > a strong 3+ wicket spell.
If nobody hit any of those, the match still gets an article - just a plain result recap with no
spotlighted individual. This was a deliberate simplification: rather than conditionally deciding
*whether* a match deserves coverage, every tournament match gets one, and milestones simply become
the headline when present. A phrase-bank of 2-3 template variants per hero-moment type (mirroring
`commentaryGenerator.js`'s established pattern) keeps the writing from feeling robotic/repetitive
across a tournament's worth of matches.

The article is stored as a `NewsPost` (`category: 'match-report'`, `isAutoGenerated: true`,
`tournament`/`match`/`heroPlayer` refs), authored by the tournament's organizer (avoids inventing a
synthetic "System" user account just for this).

### Visibility: public feed vs. personalized feed

Two different endpoints answer two different questions:
- `GET /api/news` (existing, public) - everyone can browse everything, including tournament match
  reports, like a normal news site. Extended to accept `?tournament=<id>`.
- `GET /api/news/feed` (new, auth required) - the feature the user actually asked for: general news
  plus match-report articles **only for tournaments the requesting player is registered in**,
  resolved via team membership (`Player -> Team.players -> Tournament.teams`). A player who isn't on
  any team in a given tournament won't see that tournament's articles here, even though they could
  still find them by browsing the public feed.

This split was a deliberate call: making tournament news fully private/access-gated (only
participants can see it at all) would work against a news feed's normal purpose of being
discoverable/shareable, while a purely public feed with no personalization would miss what the user
actually wanted - "if a player registered in a tournament, they should see news about it" as a real,
dedicated experience. Both needs are met without a real privacy mechanism to get wrong.

### Verification

Full curl E2E against the real running stack: registered 4 users (organizer, a hero batsman, a
"registered fan" on the opposing team in the same tournament, and an unrelated outsider), created a
tournament in `Registration` status, registered both teams, played out a match where the hero scored
exactly a century (100 off 25 balls) and their team won by 80 runs, completed the match, and
confirmed: the article auto-generated with the correct headline/body/hero attribution, the public
feed showed it, the registered fan's personalized feed showed it (`myTournaments` correctly listed
the tournament), and the outsider's personalized feed did **not** show it (only general news).

## Personalized Learn (`d396e8b`, `dc1b96a`, `dee6a09`)

New `GET /api/lessons/for-me` (auth required). Reuses `tendencyAnalytics.getBatsmanLineLengthBreakdown`
/`getBowlerLineLengthEffectiveness` - the same data already powering the shot-advice/bowling-plan
tactical insights - to find the requesting player's own worst line/length bucket (highest dismissal
rate for batting, highest economy for bowling, both gated behind the same minimum-sample-size
threshold `insightsController.js` already uses for "own-data vs generic" elsewhere in this app) and
matches it against a new free-text `tags` field on `Lesson` (drawing from the same line/length
vocabulary `Match.js`'s ball schema already enforces, e.g. `short-of-good-length`, `off-stump`).
Always returns something - pads with generic recent lessons in the player's relevant category if the
tag match comes up short, and falls back to a plain generic set with an honest `reason` string when
there's no player profile or not enough tagged-ball data yet. Same transparency pattern as the
existing insights endpoints (`source: 'own-data' | 'generic'`), not a black box.

Seeded the lesson library with 7 new tagged lessons (plus tagged 3 existing ones) covering the
line/length vocabulary gaps, authored by the existing "CricRoots Coaching" seed account, so the
feature has real content to recommend rather than only ever falling back to generic in practice.

### Verification

Curl E2E: created a lesson tagged `['off-stump', 'short-of-good-length']`, recorded 6 tagged
deliveries for a test player with 3 dismissals in that exact bucket (50% dismissal rate), and
confirmed `GET /api/lessons/for-me` returned `source: 'own-data'`, the correct human-readable reason
sentence, and the matching lesson ranked first.

## Deliberately not built

- **Global/international cricket news.** The user explicitly framed this as a future addition once
  local tournament news is solid. `NewsPost.category` already includes an unused `'international'`
  enum value as a forward-compat placeholder (no migration needed later), but nothing populates it -
  building this for real would mean either a licensed news API integration or an editorial/curation
  process, both bigger decisions than this pass should make unilaterally.
- **Lesson tagging UI beyond a simple comma-separated input** (web-app only; mobile-app's lesson
  creation flow wasn't touched) - richer tag pickers/autocomplete against the known vocabulary would
  be a nice follow-up once there's more real lesson content to justify it.
